Jia (runtime): ran a focused profile against Customer X's peak workload this morning — p99 tails jump ~3.8x when KV cold and microbatch hits 8 requests. raw traces attached (see logs).
Eli (perf-eng): can you paste the perf snapshot? curious if it's kernel switch or GC-ish.
Jia (runtime): here's the short dump: ```seq_len=2048 qps=120 microbatch=8 p95=85ms p99=420ms (kv-cold) p99=110ms (kv-warm) kernel=A32->A64 swap at step ~70```
Maya (product): customer wants "p99 <= 150ms" for their interactive flow. Sales flagged that as a hard ask for next quarter.
Sam (sales): they're in the enterprise onboarding — this p99 delta is the blocker for contract. Is this something we can fix without reducing throughput?
Eli (perf-eng): looks like two things: 1) kernel path swap under longer sequences (A32 path goes slow after cache miss) 2) large microbatches amplify queueing jitter on tails.
Jia (runtime): quick experiments: lower microbatch to 2 -> p95 90ms, p99 160ms (kv-cold). enable aggressive KV prefetch -> p99 120ms. throughput drops ~18% on that instance.
Maya (product): tradeoff conversation: customer wants p99 150ms, but they also expect 10k daily concurrent tokens (i.e., throughput). we need a clear recommendation and a concise cost delta for Sales.
Sam (sales): +1. need two options for the deck: a low-latency config (microbatch 2 + kv-prefetch + quant-kernel-restrict) and a high-throughput config (microbatch 8 + relaxed p99). numbers please.
Eli (perf-eng): propose three knobs: microbatch cap, KV warmup TTL, and kernel policy (force A32 for tail-critical flows). quick summary of measured configs: ```# baseline (mb=8, kv=default, kernel=auto): throughput=120 qps, p95=85ms, p99=420ms (cold) # low-latency (mb=2, kv=prefetch, kernel=A32): throughput=98 qps (-18%), p95=92ms, p99=130ms # balanced (mb=4, kv=aggressive, kernel=auto with no-swap): throughput=110 qps (-8%), p95=88ms, p99=165ms```
Jia (runtime): important: kernel force (A32) avoids expensive swap but increases single-token CPU usage slightly. also need to guard against long sequences where A32 runs out of optimized kernels -> will still regress.
Maya (product): can we ship a customer-specific runtime config with an SLA carveout: "tail-protection enabled" for routes X,Y with cost uplift +18%?
Eli (perf-eng): technically yes — we can pin kernel + bump prefetch TTL per-route. need to add a metric for kv-hit-rate and kernel-switch-count in Console.
Sam (sales): that's perfect. I'll propose Option A (low-latency, +18% cost) and Option B (balanced, +8% cost, p99 ~165ms) to customer. Any writeup I can paste into the SOW?
Jia (runtime): paste for SOW: "Enable per-route tail-protection: microbatch cap=2, KV prefetch=true, kernel_policy=pin-A32. Expected perf (observed): p95 ~90ms, p99 (cold) ~130ms. Throughput reduction ~18%. We recommend canarying on 10% traffic for 48h and capture kv_hit and kernel_swap metrics; rollback to balanced if error increase >0.5%"
Maya (product): add operational note: "If traffic increases >x% or seq_len distribution shifts right, re-evaluate; possible to enable hybrid routing (latency-first for small flows, throughput-first for background)."
Eli (perf-eng): action items: 1) add kernel_swap_count, kv_hit_rate dashboards (PR #4321) 2) add runtime flag to pin kernel per-route (PR #4322) 3) run 24h canary with mb=2 + kv-prefetch for Customer X (task created)
deploy-bot: started canary deployment job id=canary-8793 for customer X (mb=2, kv_prefetch=1, kernel_pin=A32)
Sam (sales): thanks everyone — I'll sync with customer tomorrow with the two options and expected uplift.
Jia (runtime): will post the full flamegraphs and traces once the canary runs for an hour. planning follow-up in #eng-runtime in ~2h. :thumbsup:
